label: cli-mistral-vibe is a member of EXECUTOR_KINDS, so a fan-out run can name Vibe as an executor kind and get an independent lineage instead of the no-kind-names-Vibe gap the phase opened with.

The kind's capability surface is narrow: it accepts only model, timeoutSeconds and liveTools, carries no reasoningEffort because Vibe has no reasoning flag, and declares no sandbox support so a sandbox request fails closed.

Model selection is closed by an enforced two-alias allowlist VIBE_SUPPORTED_MODELS = ['deepseek-flash','glm-flash'], checked by isVibeSupportedModel and rejected in config validation with a message naming the allowlist.

buildVibeLineageCommand preflights the binary, probes vibe --version in a throwaway home, refuses any version other than 3.1.2 and any off-roster model, then writes a lineage-local vibe-home seeded from .vibe/config.toml plus a trusted_folders.toml and runs vibe with --prompt-file, --output-dir, --trust, --model and --auto-approve from the lineage cwd.

The audit layer passes VIBE_-prefixed variables and MISTRAL_API_KEY to a Vibe lineage while denying an inherited VIBE_HOME, registers VIBE_HOME as lineage state with .vibe as the default home, and detects recursion on vibe, vibe-rs and vibe-app-server.

Vibe lineages are scored from export.json rather than stdout or exit status alone: success requires exit 0 with an export record whose exit_code is 0 and outcome absent or finished; exit 3 with an export record is partial; everything else is failure.

The kind is wired into the loop surface: buildVibeLineageCommand is registered in LINEAGE_COMMAND_ADAPTERS and both deep-research-auto.yaml and deep-review-auto.yaml carry an if_cli_mistral_vibe branch that fails closed with exit 2 when a single-executor run names Vibe.

The kind ships with conformance coverage: a stress fixture asserts the shipped argv shape, clean-exit success, exit-3 partial and fail-closed exit 3 without an export record, and the adapter matrix manifest registers cli-mistral-vibe.
